original_question: For integers n > 1 and r > 1, determine whether ms(S^n, I^+_2, r) = 1/r^2, where S^n is the n-dimensional sphere and I^+_2 denotes the orientation-preserving involutive isometries. Equivalently, decide whether every measurable r-coloring of S^n contains a monochromatic subset of measure at least 1/r^2 that is symmetric with respect to some line passing through the center of the sphere.
target_in_paper: Section 6, Question 6.3: the open problem asking whether the sharp value 1/r^2 remains valid for the n-dimensional sphere when one restricts symmetry to axial half-turns about lines through the center of the sphere.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual open question: it has the right space (S^n), the right parameter range (n>1 and r>1), the right candidate value (1/r^2), the measurability requirement on the coloring, and the paper's own geometric reformulation in terms of symmetry with respect to a line through the center of the sphere.
missing_details: The sphere should be understood as equipped with its normalized isometry-invariant Borel probability measure.

If the notation I_2^+ is used, it should be defined explicitly so the question is stand-alone; in this context it should denote the nontrivial involutive axial symmetries of S^n, i.e. half-turns about lines through the center.
A measurable r-coloring should be stated as a measurable map χ:S^n→{1,...,r}, equivalently a partition S^n=A_1∪⋯∪A_r into measurable color classes.

To match the paper exactly, this should be presented as an open question about whether the 1/r^2 bound is exact for this narrower symmetry family on spheres, not as an already established equivalence class of problems beyond that scope.
refined_question: For integers n>1 and r>1, let S^n be the n-dimensional sphere equipped with its normalized isometry-invariant Borel probability measure, and let I_2^+(S^n) be the family of nontrivial involutive axial symmetries of S^n, i.e. the isometries given by 180-degree rotations about lines through the center of the sphere. Is ms(S^n,I_2^+(S^n),r)=1/r^2?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, does every measurable r-coloring χ:S^n→{1,...,r} contain a monochromatic measurable subset A⊆S^n of measure at least 1/r^2 that is invariant under a half-turn about some line through the center of S^n?
justification: The nearest official formulation in the paper is Section 6, Question 6.3. The nearby Section 6 context first defines ms(Ω,S;r) for geometric objects and the relevant families of isometries, then records the general 1/r^2 result for spheres under larger symmetry families, and immediately asks whether the same value remains true when symmetry is required only with respect to a line through the center of the sphere. Your draft already captures that target almost exactly; the main things it leaves implicit are the normalized measure and a stand-alone definition of I_2^+.

citations.label: introductory definition of ms(Ω,S;r) for geometric objects and the symmetry families I, I^+, I_2, I_2^+, etc.
